text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
AUSTRALIA, April 14 - COAL - QUEENSLAND - Abbot Point - Berth vacant, 4 vessels due by 28/4, no delays.
Hay Point - One vessel loading, 13 due by 27/4, 1-2 days delay.
Dalrymple Bay - Maintenance shutdown will commence 0700 hrs. Berth closed for 88 hours and will re-open at 2300 hrs. 18/4. Two vessels loading, 2 waiting, 17 due by 26/4, 2-3 days delay.
Gladstone - R.G. Tanna - 2 Vessels loading, 5 waiting, 22 due by 17/5, 2-3 days delay.
Barney Point - Berth vacant, 2 vessels due by 24/4, no delays.
Brisbane - Six vessels due by 10/5, no delays.
NEW SOUTH WALES - Newcastle - Kooragang - 2 Vessels loading, 4 waiting, 17 due by 1/5, 3-4 days delay.
Dyke 4+5 - 2 Vessels loading, 6 waiting, 13 due by 30/4, 7-8 days delay.

Port Kembla - Two vessels loading, 1 waiting, 24 vessels due by 24/6, 1 days delay. Port Kembla port corporation pilots walked off the job on 10/4 in protest over EBA negotiations. Their case was heard by the industrial relations commission on 11/4. They were ordered to return to work while EBA negotiations continued. Normal port movements resumed at 1300 hrs. 11/4.

IRON ORE - WESTERN AUSTRALIA - Port Hedland - Mt. Newman (Nelson Point) - Due to the current shortage of fines and yandi fines, iron ore vessels may experience some delay to berthing/loading or be forced to berth out of turn. Due to the current heavy demand on lump cargo vessels, loading lump ore may experience some delays/slow loading rates (can only load one vessel with lump cargo at a time). Berth A - 1 Vessel loading, 1 anchored, 6 due by 23/4. Berth B - 1 Vessel loading, 1 anchored, 5 due by 23/4, 8 other vessels due with no eta.
Goldsworthy (Finucane Island) - 1 Vessel loading, 2 anchored, 2 due.
Dampier - Parker Point - 5 Vessels due by 16/4.
E.I. Island - 1 Vessel loading, 1 anchored, 1 due.
Dampier lineup - 1 Anchored, 20 vessels due by 1/5. A five-day maintenance shut down is planned at E.I. Island from 27/4.
Port Walcott - One vessel loading, 10 due by 27/4.
